text: manuscript’s bivariate study (two genes, two cell populations) implemented benchmark_bivariate_gaussian_convolutions() R/02_01_toy_simulation.R. purpose deliberately narrow: show even mean expression profiles similar, accounting covariance genes can () degrade standard mean-deconvolution algorithms, (b) partly alleviated DeCovarT’s native inclusion \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})=\sum_j p_j^2\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j. simplex constraint p_1+p_2=1, one free unconstrained coordinate \rho_1 needs estimated (via additive logistic map; see softmax / ALR vignette). Bulk mixtures \boldsymbol{Y}\\mathcal{M}_{G\times N} simulated without observation noise beyond Gaussian convolution : Proportions. Equi-balanced \boldsymbol{p}=(1/2,1/2) highly unbalanced \boldsymbol{p}=(0.95,0.05) (exported helper also accepts intermediate unbalanced levels (0.6,0.4)). Means. Covariances. Homoscedastic diagonals \mathrm{diag}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j)=\boldsymbol{}_2, pairwise gene–gene correlation \mathrm{Cor}(x_1,x_2) swept \{-0.8,-0.6,\ldots,0.8\} independently cell type. benchmark_bivariate_gaussian_convolutions() enumerates factorial design tidyr::expand_grid(), tags scenario unique ID, simulates N bulk replicates via simulate_bulk_mixture(), calls deconvolute_ratios() every algorithm deconvolution_functions. returned list two tibbles: config (design, Shannon entropy \boldsymbol{p}, MixSim overlap) simulations (per-sample estimates error metrics). article compares DeCovarT DeconRNASeq / NNLS (Gong Szustakowski 2013): overlap two cell-type Gaussians strong proxy estimation quality—lower overlap, lower MSE—strong gene–gene correlation fixed means inflates mean-error partially recovered \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j enters likelihood (ComplexHeatmap panels manuscript).
code: library(DeCovarT)  deconvolution_functions <- list(   "nnls" = list(FUN = deconvolute_ratios_nnls),   "lsei" = list(FUN = deconvolute_ratios_deconrnaseq),   "Marquardt-Levenberg" = list(     FUN = deconvolute_ratios_Marquardt_Levenberg,     additional_parameters = list(epsilon = 1e-3, itmax = 200)   ) )  bivariate <- benchmark_bivariate_gaussian_convolutions(   proportions = list(     "balanced" = c(0.5, 0.5),     "highly unbalanced" = c(0.95, 0.05)   ),   signature_matrices = list(     "small CLD" = matrix(c(20, 22, 22, 20), nrow = 2),     "large CLD" = matrix(c(20, 40, 40, 20), nrow = 2)   ),   corr_sequence = seq(-0.8, 0.8, by = 0.2),   diagonal_terms = list("homoscedastic" = c(1, 1)),   deconvolution_functions = deconvolution_functions,   n = 500,   cores = 1 )

title: OLS reminders for linear deconvolution
text: Dot notation: \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j} j-th column \boldsymbol{\mu}; \boldsymbol{y}_{g\cdot} g-th row. Classical texts often write design matrix \boldsymbol{X}; fixed design mean signature \boldsymbol{\mu}, MuSiC cross-subject means. Ideal noiseless model sample : \boldsymbol{y}_{\cdot }=\boldsymbol{\mu}\,\boldsymbol{p}_{\cdot }, \qquad y_{gi}=\sum_{j=1}^{J}\mu_{gj}p_{ji}. \tag{1} G>J \operatorname{rank}(\boldsymbol{\mu})=J, system overdetermined (Abbas et al. 2009); uniqueness square full-rank case follows Rouché–Capelli theorem (Shafarevich Remizov 2013).

code: # Conventional D-optimal design on a candidate grid (illustration only). # Requires the skpr package (CRAN); not used at knit time. candidates <- expand.grid(   x1 = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 11),   x2 = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 11) ) design <- skpr::gen_design(   candidateset = candidates,   model = ~ x1 + x2 + I(x1^2) + I(x2^2) + x1:x2,   trials = 20,   optimality = "D",   repeats = 100 ) skpr::get_optimality(design, "D") candidates <- expand.grid(   x1 = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 11),   x2 = seq(-1, 1, length.out = 11) ) result <- AlgDesign::optFederov(   formula = ~ x1 + x2 + I(x1^2) + I(x2^2) + x1:x2,   data = candidates,   nTrials = 20,   criterion = "D",   nRepeats = 100 ) result$D # Robust D-score for a gene panel over composition scenarios. # `information_matrices[[s]]` is I_G(p_s) for scenario s (J-1 dim.). d_objective <- function(selected, information_matrices, ridge = 1e-8) {   scores <- vapply(information_matrices, function(info_full) {     info_s <- info_full[selected, selected, drop = FALSE]     info_s <- info_s + diag(ridge, nrow(info_s))     as.numeric(determinant(info_s, logarithm = TRUE)$modulus)   }, numeric(1))   min(scores) } # Optimise the binary selection with a custom exchange / GenSA / GA.

title: Feature selection for reference-based deconvolution
text: Variance stabilisation / Pearson residuals: sctransform / Seurat::SCTransform (Hafemeister Satija 2019). Signature QC / compaction patterns: DeconvExplorer (removePercentZeros, removeUnspecificGenes, selectGenesByScore Gini entropy). Sparse multiclass candidates: glmnet multinomial elastic net (Friedman et al. 2025; Zou Hastie 2005); group penalties following (Yuan Lin 2006); stability selection (Meinshausen Bühlmann 2010). Separation monitors: MixSim::overlap() (Melnykov et al. 2024, 2012); Jeffreys via closed form Equation 13. Multi-objective panel search: mco::nsga2() (Mersmann 2024); optional scalar refinement GA / GenSA (Scrucca 2026; Gubian et al. 2025). Leakage-aware CV automation: caret workflows; pipeML custom fold construction (Hurtado Pancaldi 2026). Conventional D-optimal grids: skpr::gen_design(), AlgDesign::optFederov() (Wheeler 2025) (see Section 6.2); custom FIM + exchange / GenSA / GA (Gubian et al. 2025; Scrucca 2026) proportion-dependent DeCovarT panels. Mechanistic annotation: CARNIVAL / CORNETO (Liu et al. 2019; Rodriguez-Mier et al. 2025). Gold-standard reference-based estimators downstream validation: CIBERSORT / CIBERSORTx, EPIC, quanTIseq, ABIS, MuSiC, DWLS (Newman et al. 2015; Newman et al. 2019; Racle et al. 2017; Finotello et al. 2019; Monaco et al. 2019; Wang et al. 2019; Tsoucas et al. 2019). code: log_sum_exp <- function(z) {   m <- max(z)   m + log(sum(exp(z - m))) }  softmax <- function(z) {   exp(z - log_sum_exp(z)) } import torch import torch.nn.functional as F   def softmax(z: torch.Tensor, dim: int = -1) -> torch.Tensor:     return F.softmax(z, dim=dim)   def log_sum_exp(z: torch.Tensor, dim: int = -1) -> torch.Tensor:     return torch.logsumexp(z, dim=dim) softmax_jacobian <- function(z) {   s <- softmax(z)   diag(s) - tcrossprod(s) }  softmax_hessian <- function(z) {   s <- softmax(z)   k <- length(s)   jac <- diag(s) - tcrossprod(s)   hessian <- array(0, dim = c(k, k, k))   for (i in seq_len(k)) {     di <- (seq_len(k) == i) - s # e_i - s     hessian[i, , ] <- s[i] * (tcrossprod(di) - jac)   }   hessian } def softmax_jacobian(z: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """z: [..., K] -> [..., K, K]."""     s = softmax(z, dim=-1)     return torch.diag_embed(s) - s.unsqueeze(-1) * s.unsqueeze(-2)   def softmax_hessian(z: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """z: [K] -> H[i, j, k] of shape [K, K, K]."""     s = softmax(z, dim=0)     eye = torch.eye(s.numel(), dtype=s.dtype, device=s.device)     diff = eye - s  # (e_i - s) stacked over i     outer = diff.unsqueeze(-1) * diff.unsqueeze(-2)     jac = torch.diag(s) - torch.outer(s, s)     return s[:, None, None] * (outer - jac.unsqueeze(0))

log_p[..., -1:] additive_logistic_jacobian <- function(rho) {   p <- additive_logistic(rho)   j <- length(p)   (diag(p) - tcrossprod(p))[, -j, drop = FALSE] }  additive_logistic_hessian <- function(rho) {   p <- additive_logistic(rho)   j <- length(p)   jac <- diag(p) - tcrossprod(p)   hessian <- array(0, dim = c(j, j - 1, j - 1))   for (i in seq_len(j)) {     di <- (seq_len(j) == i) - p     slice <- p[i] * (tcrossprod(di) - jac)     hessian[i, , ] <- slice[-j, -j]   }   hessian } def additive_logistic_jacobian(rho: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """rho: [J-1] -> Jacobian [J, J-1]."""     p = additive_logistic(rho)     return (torch.diag(p) - torch.outer(p, p))[:, :-1]   def additive_logistic_hessian(rho: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """rho: [J-1] -> Hessian [J, J-1, J-1]."""     reference = torch.zeros_like(rho[:1])     augmented = torch.cat([rho, reference])     return softmax_hessian(augmented)[:, :-1, :-1] additive_log_ratio_jacobian <- function(p) {   j <- length(p)   idx <- seq_len(j - 1)   jac <- matrix(0, j - 1, j)   jac[cbind(idx, idx)] <- 1 / p[idx]   jac[, j] <- -1 / p[j]   jac }  additive_log_ratio_hessian <- function(p) {   j <- length(p)   hessian <- array(0, dim = c(j - 1, j, j))   for (i in seq_len(j - 1)) {     hessian[i, i, i] <- -1 / p[i]^2     hessian[i, j, j] <- 1 / p[j]^2   }   hessian } def additive_log_ratio_jacobian(p: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """p: [J] -> Jacobian [J-1, J]."""     j = p.numel()     jac = torch.zeros(j - 1, j, dtype=p.dtype, device=p.device)     idx = torch.arange(j - 1, device=p.device)     jac[idx, idx] = 1.0 / p[:-1]     jac[:, -1] = -1.0 / p[-1]     return jac   def additive_log_ratio_hessian(p: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """p: [J] -> Hessian [J-1, J, J]."""     j = p.numel()     hessian = torch.zeros(j - 1, j, j, dtype=p.dtype, device=p.device)     idx = torch.arange(j - 1, device=p.device)     hessian[idx, idx, idx] = -1.0 / p[:-1].square()     hessian[:, -1, -1] = 1.0 / p[-1].square()     return hessian

code: additive_logistic_jacobian <- function(rho) {   p <- additive_logistic(rho)   j <- length(p)   (diag(p) - tcrossprod(p))[, -j, drop = FALSE] }  additive_logistic_hessian <- function(rho) {   p <- additive_logistic(rho)   j <- length(p)   jac <- diag(p) - tcrossprod(p)   hessian <- array(0, dim = c(j, j - 1, j - 1))   for (i in seq_len(j)) {     di <- (seq_len(j) == i) - p     slice <- p[i] * (tcrossprod(di) - jac)     hessian[i, , ] <- slice[-j, -j]   }   hessian } def additive_logistic_jacobian(rho: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """rho: [J-1] -> Jacobian [J, J-1]."""     p = additive_logistic(rho)     return (torch.diag(p) - torch.outer(p, p))[:, :-1]   def additive_logistic_hessian(rho: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """rho: [J-1] -> Hessian [J, J-1, J-1]."""     reference = torch.zeros_like(rho[:1])     augmented = torch.cat([rho, reference])     return softmax_hessian(augmented)[:, :-1, :-1]

title: Simplex maps and numerically stable softmax / ALR derivatives
text: Treating \boldsymbol{p} ambient coordinates \mathbb{R}^{J} (admissible tangent directions satisfy \sum_i \mathrm{d}p_i=0), alr Jacobian \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{alr}}\\mathcal{M}_{(J-1)\times J} sparse, \frac{\partial\rho_i}{\partial p_j}=\frac{\delta_{ij}}{p_i}-\frac{\delta_{jJ}}{p_J}, \qquad \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{alr}} =\Bigl[\operatorname{diag}\!\bigl(p_1^{-1},\ldots,p_{J-1}^{-1}\bigr) \ \big|\ -p_J^{-1}\boldsymbol{1}_{J-1}\Bigr], \tag{11} Hessian \mathbf{H}_{\mathrm{alr}}\\mathcal{M}_{(J-1)\times J\times J} diagonal last two modes, \frac{\partial^2\rho_i}{\partial p_j\partial p_k} =-\frac{\delta_{ij}\delta_{ik}}{p_i^{2}} +\frac{\delta_{jJ}\delta_{kJ}}{p_J^{2}}. \tag{12} Listing 9: Jacobian Hessian additive log-ratio map R Listing 10: Jacobian Hessian additive log-ratio map PyTorch
code: additive_log_ratio_jacobian <- function(p) {   j <- length(p)   idx <- seq_len(j - 1)   jac <- matrix(0, j - 1, j)   jac[cbind(idx, idx)] <- 1 / p[idx]   jac[, j] <- -1 / p[j]   jac }  additive_log_ratio_hessian <- function(p) {   j <- length(p)   hessian <- array(0, dim = c(j - 1, j, j))   for (i in seq_len(j - 1)) {     hessian[i, i, i] <- -1 / p[i]^2     hessian[i, j, j] <- 1 / p[j]^2   }   hessian } def additive_log_ratio_jacobian(p: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """p: [J] -> Jacobian [J-1, J]."""     j = p.numel()     jac = torch.zeros(j - 1, j, dtype=p.dtype, device=p.device)     idx = torch.arange(j - 1, device=p.device)     jac[idx, idx] = 1.0 / p[:-1]     jac[:, -1] = -1.0 / p[-1]     return jac   def additive_log_ratio_hessian(p: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:     """p: [J] -> Hessian [J-1, J, J]."""     j = p.numel()     hessian = torch.zeros(j - 1, j, j, dtype=p.dtype, device=p.device)     idx = torch.arange(j - 1, device=p.device)     hessian[idx, idx, idx] = -1.0 / p[:-1].square()     hessian[:, -1, -1] = 1.0 / p[-1].square()     return hessian

text: analytic maps half usable optimiser: Newton-type iteration also evaluates Gaussian-convolution log-likelihood derivatives respect \boldsymbol{p} (\boldsymbol{\rho}). Several practical bottlenecks numerical inconsistencies showed running hybrid scenario Deconvolution use cases; changes live R/03_03_DeCovarT_estimate_ratios_frequentist.R. deconvolute_ratios_Newton_Raphson() wraps stats::nlminb(). earlier control list set eval.max = 1, caps total number objective evaluations whole run (per iteration). solver therefore evaluated log-likelihood equi-balanced start stopped, returning untouched initial guess every sample. Removing entry (keeping iter.max, rel.tol, ) restores genuine Newton steps; see /contrast (Newton_Raphson versus Newton_Raphson_fixed) Table solver diagnostics. Within one iteration, optim() / nlminb() / marqLevAlg() treat log-likelihood, gradient Hessian independent callbacks, yet hit trial \boldsymbol{p}. Assembling \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})=\sum_j p_j^2\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j factorising separately callback (inside constrained Hessian chain rule) paid O(G^3) factorisation four times per iteration. internal helper .sigma_p_factorisation() caches single Cholesky factor keyed exact equality (p, Sigma) returns \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p}) = \mathbf{R}^{\mathsf{T}}\mathbf{R}, \qquad \log\det\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p}) = 2\sum_{g=1}^{G}\log R_{gg}, \qquad \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})^{-1} = \mathbf{R}^{-1}(\mathbf{R}^{\mathsf{T}})^{-1} \tag{13} via chol() / chol2inv() (Eq. 13). unconstrained log-likelihood uses cached log-determinant inverse, \ell_{\boldsymbol{y}\,|\,\boldsymbol{\zeta}}(\boldsymbol{p}) = -\log\det\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p}) -\tfrac{1}{2} \boldsymbol{r}^{\mathsf{T}} \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})^{-1} \boldsymbol{r}, \qquad \boldsymbol{r} = \boldsymbol{y}-\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p}, \tag{14} gradient_loglik_unconstrained() hessian_loglik_unconstrained() reuse \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})^{-1} (Eq. 14). Analytic gradients Hessians still match numDeriv \sim 10^{-8}–10^{-9} refactor. deconvolute_ratios_L_BFGS_B() optimises directly \boldsymbol{p} box constraints [0,1]^J. boxes alone enforce \mathbf{1}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{p}=1, line searches can drive \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p}) singular. objective analytic gradient wrapped: near \sum_j p_j\approx 0 (failed chol()), log-likelihood returns finite penalty gradient zero vector rather aborting optim(): solver previously relied finite-difference gradients. Passing gr = safe_gradient (unconstrained analytic score) removes cost keeps safeguarded behaviour . Caution 1: marqLevAlg(minimize = FALSE) flip hess marqLevAlg (Philipps et al. 2023) implements Marquardt–Levenberg algorithm relative-distance--minimum (RDM) stopping rule Commenges et al. (Commenges et al. 2006): C_k \approx m^{-1} \boldsymbol{U}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_k)^{\mathsf{T}} \mathbf{G}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_k)^{-1} \boldsymbol{U}(\boldsymbol{\theta}_k). \tag{15} minimize = FALSE, package negates user-supplied fn gr. analytic hess passed unchanged, internal Cholesky / inversion routines (dsinv, dchole) assume positive-definite matrix optimum (minimisation convention). maximising log-likelihood, hessian_loglik_constrained() negative-definite MLE, dsinv fails (ier = -1) every iteration, rdm sticks unevaluated sentinel epsd + 1 (e.g. 1.0001), algorithm always exhausts maxiter (istop = 2) even iterate already maximum. Workaround used DeCovarT: pass hess = function(...) -hessian_loglik_constrained(...) keep minimize = FALSE. Reported upstream VivianePhilipps/marqLevAlgParallel#3. Table 3 summarises empirical confirmation hybrid J=3 scenario (m=J-1=2 free ALR coordinates). Point estimates barely moved (wrongly scaled Newton step often rescued internal line search), iterations dropped roughly 20–40\times istop / rdm became honest relative Eq. 15. Table 3: Effect negating analytic Hessian passed marqLevAlg maximize = TRUE (minimize = FALSE).
code: safe_loglik <- function(p, y, mean_signature_matrix, Sigma) {   if (sum(p) < 1e-8) {     return(-1e12)   }   tryCatch(     loglik_multivariate(p, y, mean_signature_matrix, Sigma),     error = function(e) -1e12   ) } safe_gradient <- function(p, y, mean_signature_matrix, Sigma) {   if (sum(p) < 1e-8) {     return(rep(0, length(p)))   }   tryCatch(     gradient_loglik_unconstrained(p, y, mean_signature_matrix, Sigma),     error = function(e) rep(0, length(p))   ) }

title: Simulating semi-synthetic pseudo-bulk mixtures for benchmarking
text: vignette documents synthetic first- second-order moment generator simulate_hierarchical_grn_moments() outputs feed bulk mixture simulation. Mean profiles follow AutoGeneS-inspired construction (Aliee Theis 2021) single dial \rho (target_cosine) sets pairwise collinearity cell-type columns \boldsymbol{\mu}, fixed scale s (mean_scale) sets column norms. Prefer varying \rho across scenarios precision weights already control second-order dependence. cell type carries graph-constrained signed precision \boldsymbol{\Omega}_j, mapped \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j=\boldsymbol{\Omega}_j^{-1}. undirected Gaussian Markov simulation separates four layers (Equation 12): graph G_j, signed weights W(G_j), SPD precision \Omega_j, latent Gaussians (optional observation layer can add Poisson–log-normal zero-inflated counts). graph precision must conflated: binary adjacency almost never positive definite. DeCovarT draws G_j via generate_random_network_skeleton(), completes \Omega_j\succ 0 build_normalised_precision(), stacks inverted slices build_covariance_array_from_precision(). Section 4 develops topology, weight, SPD design detail.

text: Constrained DeCovarT maps unconstrained coordinates \boldsymbol{\rho}_{}\\mathbb{R}^{J-1} cellular proportions \boldsymbol{p}_{} open simplex via regularised soft-max \boldsymbol{\psi}, forms bulk observation Gaussian convolution cell-type profiles \boldsymbol{x}_{j}\sim\mathcal{N}_{G}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{j},\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j}): \boldsymbol{y}_{}\,|\,\cdot \sim\mathcal{N}_{G}\!\Bigl(   \boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p}_{},\;   \sum_{j=1}^{J}p_{ji}^{2}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j} \Bigr). diagram shows constrained graphical model. Forward map \boldsymbol{\psi}:\boldsymbol{\rho}\mapsto\boldsymbol{p} (C^{2}-diffeomorphism): p_{j}=\frac{e^{\rho_{j}}}{\sum_{k<J}e^{\rho_{k}}+1}\ (j<J),\qquad p_{J}=\frac{1}{\sum_{k<J}e^{\rho_{k}}+1},\qquad \boldsymbol{\psi}^{-1}(\boldsymbol{p})=\bigl(\ln(p_{j}/p_{J})\bigr)_{j<J}.

what: Additive logistic transform (unconstrained coordinates to the simplex) — additive_logistic
title: Additive logistic transform (unconstrained coordinates to the simplex) — additive_logistic
text: Implements reparametrisation \(\boldsymbol{\psi}:\boldsymbol{\rho}\mapsto\boldsymbol{p}\) used article, sending unconstrained coordinates \(\boldsymbol{\rho}\\mathbb{R}^{J-1}\) cellular proportions \(\boldsymbol{p}\\Delta^{J-1}\). additive logistic transform Aitchison, .e. inverse additive log-ratio map (\(\mathrm{alr}^{-1}\)), equivalently softmax last category \(J\) pinned reference (\(\rho_J\equiv 0\)). Recovers unconstrained additive log-ratio coordinates \(\rho_j=\ln(p_j/p_J)\) \(j=1,\ldots,J-1\), last part \(p_J\) reference. Aitchison's additive log-ratio (\(\mathrm{alr}\)) transform, equivalently multinomial-logit link reference category \(J\) (see compositions::alr() vignette("softmax-alr-derivatives", package = "DeCovarT")).

text: Returns \(p_j p_{\ell}\)-weighted mean pairwise Jeffreys (symmetrised KL) divergences purified Gaussians $$   \overline{J}   =   \frac{     \sum_{1\le j<\ell\le J} p_j p_{\ell}\, J(f_{j},f_{\ell})   }{     \sum_{1\le j<\ell\le J} p_j p_{\ell}   }   \[0,\infty), $$ \(f_{j}=\mathcal{N}_{G}(   \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j},\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{j} )\). p omitted defaults equi-balanced vector \(1/J\), recovers uniform pairwise average \(2/(J(J-1))\sum_{j<\ell}J(f_{j},f_{\ell})\).

text: Computes two objectives used AutoGeneS signature quality. columns \(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j},\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}\) \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\), cosine (angle similarity, akin Pearson correlation centred, unit-norm vectors without mean-centring—\(\ell_2\) normalisation) $$   \cos(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j},\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k})   =   \frac{     \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}^{\mathsf{T}}     \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}   }{     \|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}\|_2\,     \|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}\|_2   }, $$ Euclidean separation $$   \|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}-\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}\|_2   =   \sqrt{     \|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}\|_2^{2}     +\|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}\|_2^{2}     -2\,     \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}^{\mathsf{T}}     \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}   }. $$ returned scores mean absolute pairwise cosine (minimise) sum pairwise Euclidean distances (maximise).

what: Normalised Shannon entropy of a discrete distribution — compute_shannon_entropy
title: Normalised Shannon entropy of a discrete distribution — compute_shannon_entropy
text: probability vector \(\boldsymbol{p}\\Delta^{J-1}\) \(J\) classes (: cell types), Shannon entropy $$   H(\boldsymbol{p})   =   -\sum_{j=1}^{J} p_j \log p_j, $$ convention \(0\log 0 = 0\). Dividing maximum entropy \(\log J\) (uniform \(J\) classes) yields Pielou's evenness $$   H^{\star}(\boldsymbol{p})   =   \frac{H(\boldsymbol{p})}{\log J}   \[0,1], $$ \(H^{\star}=0\) Dirac mass one type \(H^{\star}=1\) uniform distribution \(J\) cell types. Zero masses dropped inside sum; normaliser still uses original class count \(J\). preferable changing logarithm base number positive masses \(J'\), renormalise support hide sparsity relative full panel cell types.

title: DeCovarT MLE of cellular proportions for one bulk sample — deconvolute_ratios_cibersort
text: Estimates \(\hat{\boldsymbol{p}}=\arg\max_{\boldsymbol{p}} \ell_{\boldsymbol{y}\,|\,\boldsymbol{\zeta}}(\boldsymbol{p})\) Gaussian convolution model $$   \boldsymbol{y}\,|\,(\boldsymbol{\zeta},\boldsymbol{p})   \sim\mathcal{N}_{G}\!\bigl(\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p},\,   \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})\bigr),   \qquad   \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})=\sum_{j=1}^{J}p_j^{2}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j, $$ subject simplex constraint \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{p}=1\), \(\boldsymbol{p}\ge\mathbf{0}\). Optimisation performed unconstrained coordinates \(\boldsymbol{\rho}\\mathbb{R}^{J-1}\) via \(\boldsymbol{p}=\boldsymbol{\psi}(\boldsymbol{\rho})\) (Marquardt–Levenberg default; see methods vignette("softmax-alr-derivatives", package = "DeCovarT")).

what: Generate mean profiles with a target pairwise cosine — generate_mean_signature_matrix
title: Generate mean profiles with a target pairwise cosine — generate_mean_signature_matrix
text: Builds \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\\mathcal{M}_{G\times J}\) blending shared unit direction \(\boldsymbol{u}\) cell-type-private orthogonal marker directions \(\boldsymbol{v}_{j}\): $$   \tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}   =   \sqrt{\rho}\,\boldsymbol{u}   +\sqrt{1-\rho}\,\boldsymbol{v}_{j},   \qquad   \boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}   =   s\,   \frac{\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}}{     \|\tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}\|_2   }. $$ private vectors \(\boldsymbol{v}_{j}\) indicator directions partition \(G\) genes (type \(j\) ) \(\ell_2\)-normalised, \(\boldsymbol{v}_{j}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{v}_{k}=0\) \(j\neq k\). shared unit \(\boldsymbol{u}\), $$   \tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}^{\mathsf{T}}   \tilde{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot k}   =   \rho   +   \sqrt{\rho(1-\rho)}\,   \bigl(     \boldsymbol{u}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{v}_{j}     +     \boldsymbol{u}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{v}_{k}   \bigr)   \qquad (j\neq k). $$ column normalisation pairwise cosines \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) therefore track \(\rho\) closely cross terms \(\boldsymbol{u}^{\mathsf{T}}\boldsymbol{v}_{j}\) small relative leading \(\rho\) (many genes per block). global scale \(s\) sets column norms (hence Euclidean separation) without changing angles: fixed \(\rho\), \(\|\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}-\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot k}\|_2 \propto s\). Prefer dialling \(\rho\) second-order precision weights already control interaction strength; keep \(s\) fixed across scenarios compare mean collinearity alone (Aliee Theis 2021) .

title: Generate mean profiles with a target pairwise cosine — generate_mean_signature_matrix
text: Private marker blocks. Genes partitioned \(J\) nearly equal contiguous blocks. Type \(j\)'s private direction \(\boldsymbol{v}_{j}\) indicator block, \(\ell_2\)-normalised. Distinct blocks orthogonal, type-specific signal leak across columns shared component added. Shared–private blend. unit shared direction \(\boldsymbol{u}=G^{-1/2}\mathbf{1}\), column \(\sqrt{\rho}\,\boldsymbol{u}+\sqrt{1-\rho}\,\boldsymbol{v}_{j}\), re-normalised, scaled \(s\). what: Simulate bulk mixtures from a multivariate Gaussian convolution — simulate_bulk_mixture
title: Simulate bulk mixtures from a multivariate Gaussian convolution — simulate_bulk_mixture
text: bootstrap sample \(=1,\ldots,N\), draws latent purified profiles \(\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot j}^{()}\sim\mathcal{N}_{G}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\cdot j}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j)\) independently cell type \(j=1,\ldots,J\), forms bulk linear convolution $$   \boldsymbol{y}_{\cdot }   =\boldsymbol{X}^{()}\boldsymbol{p}   =\sum_{j=1}^{J}p_j\,\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot j}^{()}, $$ matching article's conditional model \(\boldsymbol{y}\,|\,(\boldsymbol{\zeta},\boldsymbol{p})\sim \mathcal{N}_{G}(\boldsymbol{\mu}\boldsymbol{p}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p}))\) \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p})= \sum_j p_j^{2}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_j\). mean signature \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\) shared across samples; latent draws \(\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot j}^{()}\) vary \(\). Stacking draws three-way array \(\mathcal{X}=(x_{gji})\\mathcal{M}_{G\times J\times N}\), bulk matrix mode-2 tensor–vector contraction $$   \boldsymbol{Y}   =\mathcal{X}\times_{2}\boldsymbol{p},   \qquad   y_{gi}=\sum_{j=1}^{J}x_{gji}\,p_{j}   \quad(g=1,\ldots,G;\; =1,\ldots,N), $$ sample recovers \(\boldsymbol{y}_{\cdot }=\boldsymbol{X}^{()}\,\boldsymbol{p}\) \(\boldsymbol{X}^{()}\\mathcal{M}_{G\times J}\).

title: DeCovarT 2.0.0
text: Release aligned GitHub v2.0.0 tag first CRAN submission, focused numerical stability optimiser cost R/03_03_DeCovarT_estimate_ratios_frequentist.R (documented vignette("softmax-alr-derivatives"), section Numerical speed-ups solver safeguards). CRAN tarball ships use-cases softmax/ALR vignettes; remaining articles stay pkgdown site. Newton–Raphson evaluation budget. Removed erroneous eval.max = 1 control passed stats::nlminb() deconvolute_ratios_Newton_Raphson(), capped entire run single objective evaluation silently returned equi-balanced start. Cached Cholesky factorisation \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p}). New internal .sigma_p_factorisation() assembles mixture covariance per trial point, shares chol() / chol2inv() across log-likelihood, gradient Hessian, uses Cholesky-based log-determinant (verified numDeriv). Analytic gradient L-BFGS-B. deconvolute_ratios_L_BFGS_B() now passes unconstrained analytic score instead finite differences, finite-penalty guards box-constrained line searches drive \boldsymbol{\Sigma}(\boldsymbol{p}) near-singular. marqLevAlg Hessian sign maximisation. minimize = FALSE, marqLevAlg negates fn / gr; analytic Hessian must negated hand Commenges et al. RDM criterion can fire. Reported upstream VivianePhilipps/marqLevAlgParallel#3. Documentation. Expanded use-cases feature-selection vignettes; CRAN-oriented DESCRIPTION (MIT licence, arXiv method reference doi:10.48550/arXiv.2309.09557).

title: DeCovarT 1.0.0
text: First stabilised release DeCovarT (semver 1.0.0), marking end exploratory 0.x series. core ALR-based frequentist deconvolution API, analytic score equations, simulation tooling now treated stable public surface downstream use paper reproduction. Analytic derivatives, numerically verified. unconstrained constrained log-likelihood gradients Hessians (additive logistic Jacobian / Hessian) derived closed form unit-tested numDeriv finite differences. Earlier faulty numerical / finite-difference-paths mislead Marquardt–Levenberg related optimisers replaced verified analytic expressions (see vignette("softmax-alr-derivatives") tests/testthat/test-03_03_DeCovarT.R). Simulation framework beyond bivariate toy. Synthetic first- second-order moments now support arbitrary gene panels (G\gg 2) multi-type mixtures: AutoGeneS-style mean signatures cosine dial, graph-constrained precisions (ER, hub/star, scale-free, SBM, small-world), bulk convolution via simulate_bulk_mixture(). hybrid multi-topology reference scenario (G=50, J=3) scripts/generate_random_markov_network.R vignette("synthetic-scenarios") stresses feature selection EE / DE / differential-modality-like blocks (scDD / muscat-inspired taxonomy). Feature-selection metrics (compute_average_overlap(), compute_average_jeffreys(), compute_glmnet_gene_scores()) shared check_true_theta() validator complete end--end simulation → pre-screen → NSGA-II refinement loop documented vignette("feature-selection").
